_style: Drawn as a clean 3D game-asset concept render in a stylised anime background-art style: simple confident shapes, flat hand-painted colours with one soft shadow tone, crisp edges, no photographic noise. The WHOLE object is in frame with margin on every side, centred on a plain pure white background. Soft even studio light, no cast shadow on the ground, no reflections, no people, no text, no lettering, no writing in any language, no numbers, no logos, no brand badges, no watermark.
CafeTableTop: A small cafe table setting on a round wooden serving tray 40 centimetres across: two white coffee cups on saucers, one with latte art, a small teal glass vase holding three pink flowers, and a tiny plate with a cookie. Everything chunky and simple, sitting on the tray. Seen from a three-quarter view from above.
CafeWallArt: A group of three framed pictures hung in a row on a wall, the whole group 1.7 metres wide and 65 centimetres tall: a large landscape frame in the middle and a smaller portrait frame on each side, all in thick honey-coloured wooden frames joined by one thin wooden rail along the top. Each picture is a simple abstract design in flat blocks of teal, cream, coral and mustard, like cut paper shapes: a sun over hills, a coffee cup shape, and a leaf. Seen straight from the front.
CafeClock: A round cafe wall clock 34 centimetres across with a thick honey-coloured wooden rim, a cream face with twelve plain short tick marks and no numerals, and two bold black hands set to ten past ten. Seen from the front, turned very slightly to one side so its thickness shows.
CafeRug: A rectangular cafe floor rug 2.6 metres long and 1.8 metres wide, thick and flat, lying on the floor: a woven rug with a wide teal border, a cream field and a simple geometric pattern of coral and mustard diamonds, with a short fringe at the two short ends. Seen from above at an angle so the whole rectangle is visible.
CafeAwning: A shop awning for over a cafe door, 4 metres wide, projecting 1.3 metres from the wall and sloping gently downward toward the street: taut canvas in wide teal and cream stripes with a scalloped valance hanging along the front edge, carried on a slim black steel frame with two folding side arms. No writing on it. Seen from a three-quarter front view from slightly below.
Noren: A Japanese shop doorway curtain, the short split kind hung across the top of a door, 1.5 metres wide and 1 metre tall: four hanging panels of thick indigo-blue cloth with a simple white pattern of three circles and a wave line, threaded on a round wooden pole that sticks out a little at each end. No characters, no letters. Seen straight from the front, panels hanging flat.
